newsitem.title: USA: Air cargo growth put at 7.9 pct a year to 2005.
newsitem.headline: Air cargo growth put at 7.9 pct a year to 2005.

text.p: Air cargo traffic worldwide is expected to grow by 7.9 percent in revenue ton miles annually through 2000, the consultancy MergeGlobe Inc. said on Thursday.

MergeGlobe principal Brian Clancy told a Federal Aviation Administration conference that growth for 1990-1995 was 8.2 percent. The FAA said 1996 growth for U.S. carriers was up 4.2 percent over 1995, but issued no global growth figure.
Clancy said detailed cargo forecasts are not made because of the changing nature of manufacturing and the factors that go into decisions whether to ship goods by air, sea, rail or truck.
He said manufacturers are increasingly using global sourcing for components, are relying more on just-in-time supply and are making wider use single shippers for all modes of transport.

Clancy added that decisions whether to use air to ship is based on changing factors such a product value to weight ratio, whether it is physically perishable, such as flowers, or economically perishable, such a clothes for Christmas sales, and an unpredictable demand for goods such as spare parts or the latest version of a computer.
Global forecasts issued earlier by Boeing Co. predict an increase of 6.6 percent a year and by McDonnell Douglas Corp. of 7.4 percent, both through 2005.
